summary.summary:
## Background
- Study population: 82 Chilean adults with advanced colorectal cancer treated with 5‑fluorouracil (5‑FU)–based regimens (often with oxaliplatin or irinotecan).
- Aim: Evaluate 16 variants across TYMS, TYMP, DPYD, GSTP1, MTHFR, ERCC2, ABCB1/2/4, and ABCG2 to identify genetic predictors of chemotherapy toxicities and build preliminary risk models.

## Key Findings
- GSTP1 c.313A>G (rs1695)
  - G allele reduced risk of neuropathy (OR 0.147; p=0.012) and broadly lowered nervous system and hematologic toxicities (e.g., hematologic, dominant model OR 0.298; p=0.001; recessive OR 0.157; p=0.0005).
  - G allele increased risk of mucositis (OR 2.27; p=0.036).

- DPYD c.85T>C (rs1801265; DPYD*9)
  - C allele increased neuropathy risk (dominant model OR 4.58; p=0.05; codominant T/C OR 30.0; p=0.0049 in sensitivity analysis).
  - Canonical DPYD loss‑of‑function variants (DPYD*2A rs3918290 and DPYD*13 rs55886062) were monomorphic in this cohort and not analyzable.

- TYMS
  - 3′UTR 6‑bp ins/del (rs11280056): the deletion genotype markedly reduced hematologic toxicity (OR 0.029; p=0.001) and was protective for gastrointestinal toxicity; it also lowered severe hematologic events (dominant OR 0.098; p=0.005).
  - 5′UTR VNTR (rs45445694): 3R/3R increased risk of skin/subcutaneous disorders (OR 6.40; p=0.029).

- ERCC2 c.2251A>C (rs13181)
  - C/C genotype associated with lower gastrointestinal toxicity (OR 0.10; p=0.045).
  - In a multivariable pain model, C/C increased pain risk (OR 6.27; p=0.034), highlighting phenotype‑specific effects.

- TYMP c.1412C>T (rs11479)
  - T allele associated with higher pain risk; in an anemia model, T/T strongly predicted anemia (OR 23.76; p=0.038).

- MTHFR
  - rs1801131 (A1298C): C‑carrier status reduced pain risk (dominant OR 0.375; p=0.048) but increased risk of nervous system disorders (dominant OR 5.81; p=0.035); in a pain model, C‑carrier remained protective (OR 0.159; p=0.034).
  - rs1801133 (C677T): C allele associated with higher nervous system toxicity and lower pain risk (reported in text; stats in supplementary data).

- ABCB1
  - rs1128503 (c.1236T>C): C/C increased pain (recessive OR 4.20; p=0.049).
  - rs1045642 (c.3435C>T): contributed to an anemia model (model p=0.027; AUC ≈0.71) but was not independently significant.

- Multivariable models
  - Anemia: TYMP rs11479 (T/T) + ABCB1 rs1045642 predicted risk (model p=0.027; AUC ~0.71), driven by TYMP.
  - Pain: ERCC2 rs13181 (C/C; OR 6.27; p=0.034) + MTHFR rs1801131 (A/C+C/C; OR 0.159; p=0.034) predicted risk (model p=0.01; AUC ~0.75).

## Clinical Implications
- Beyond standard DPYD loss‑of‑function testing, additional variants may refine toxicity risk in 5‑FU/oxaliplatin regimens:
  - Consider GSTP1 rs1695 to identify patients at lower neuropathy but higher mucositis risk, potentially guiding oxaliplatin exposure and mucositis prophylaxis.
  - DPYD rs1801265 C carriers may warrant heightened neuropathy monitoring and oxaliplatin dose vigilance.
  - TYMS rs11280056 deletion identifies patients at lower risk for hematologic (including severe) and GI toxicities; TYMS rs45445694 3R/3R flags higher skin toxicity risk.
  - ERCC2 rs13181 and MTHFR rs1801131 together may stratify pain risk; TYMP rs11479 T/T flags anemia and pain susceptibility; ABCB1 rs1128503 C/C flags pain risk.
- These findings are exploratory (single‑center, n=82) and population‑specific; prospective validation is needed before routine implementation. They provide a foundation for integrating multi‑gene panels with clinical factors to individualize dosing, supportive care, and monitoring in Chilean (and potentially similar) CRC populations.
